FACT_ID: sec10-R01 | anchor: A01
Headlight distances differ by purpose: lights on when visibility is under 1,000 feet, dim for oncoming traffic within 500 feet, low beams when following within 200 feet. [A01]
Why it matters: group night driving; difficulty three; confusable sec10-F10 vs sec10-F13 vs sec10-F14. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec10-R02 | anchor: A01
Parking lights are required on a vehicle parked at the roadside at night, but driving with only parking lights on is not allowed. [A01]
Why it matters: group night driving; difficulty two; prereq sec10-F11. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec10-R03 | anchor: A01
High beams help on dark open highways but backfire in fog, where low beams or fog lights work better. [A01]
Why it matters: group night driving; difficulty two; confusable sec10-F12 vs sec10-F16. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec10-R04 | anchor: A01
In a hydroplane you steer gently toward the direction of the slide, not away from it, and you ease off the gas instead of braking. [A01]
Why it matters: group weather; difficulty three; prereq sec10-F23 and sec10-F24. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec10-R05 | anchor: A01
In a curve you slow down before entry and accelerate only after the middle, never while entering. [A01]
Why it matters: group hills and curves; difficulty two; prereq sec10-F08. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec10-R06 | anchor: A01
The no-passing distance near intersections and railroad crossings is 100 feet, the same figure used for bridges, viaducts and tunnels with a blocked view. [A01]
Why it matters: group passing; difficulty two; prereq sec10-F01 and sec10-F05. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec10-R07 | anchor: A01
Four-wheel or all-wheel drive does not exempt you from slowing down and adding following distance in bad weather. [A01]
Why it matters: group weather; difficulty two; prereq sec10-F19. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0019]

Misconception: cruise control helps keep steady on wet or icy highways; do not use it there. [A01]
Misconception: a flooded road can be crossed if taken slowly; find another route instead. [A01]
Misconception: looking straight at oncoming headlights keeps you aware; drop your eyes below the glare and follow the painted edge lines instead. [A01]
Misconception: dawn and dusk are as easy as daytime driving; they can be more hazardous than daytime. [A01]
Mnemonic: Slow down, back off: the two weather rules. [A01]
Mnemonic: Fog loves low beams, high beams make a mirror. [A01]
Glossary: Hydroplaning means tires riding on a layer of water so traction and steering are lost. [A01]
Glossary: Cresting a hill means reaching its top where the road beyond comes back into view. [A01]
Glossary: Overcorrecting means jerking the wheel too far while regaining control. [A01]
